# Llama 3 70B - MI300X Analysis

## Executive Summary

A single-rank PyTorch trace of Llama 3 70B (BF16, GQA 8:1, sequence length 8192) on MI300X spends 99.30% of GPU time in computation, with negligible idle (0.25%) and exposed communication (0.42%). The workload is dominated by BF16 GEMMs (80.6% of compute time) which run at 68.7%–86.7% of the 708 TFLOPS BF16 matrix peak — leaving meaningful matrix-FP headroom on the dominant matmul cluster. Flash Attention forward and backward kernels (CK backend) consume an additional ~13% of compute and run well below their expected efficiency band (37% and 55% of peak respectively). System-level pipeline health is strong (98.6% compute/communication overlap), so the optimization frontier is on per-kernel matrix throughput.

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Total Time | 56703.68 ms |
| Compute % | 99.30% |
| Idle % | 0.25% |
| Exposed Communication % | 0.42% |
| Top Bottleneck Category | GEMM (81.18%) |

### 🔴 P1: Compute-bound BF16 GEMMs underrunning roofline (Tensile)

**Insight**: 18 BF16 `aten::mm` shapes are compute-bound and run at 68.7%–86.7% of the 708 TFLOPS BF16 MAF peak, leaving meaningful headroom on the dominant matmul workload.

**Action**: Profile the dominant member kernels for tile-size and wave-occupancy tuning. If the model tolerates a narrower precision than BF16 (e.g. FP8/FP4), narrow the precision to lower the compute floor; the smallest shapes (count = 2) amortize launch overhead poorly and can be batched upstream.

### 🔴 P1: H2D memcpy hygiene check

**Insight**: 490 H2D transfers are issued per profile window, but their aggregate time (0.03% of E2E) is fully hidden behind compute and is not on the critical path.

**Action**: No code change required for performance. As a hygiene check, confirm host buffers feeding these transfers are page-locked (pinned) and submitted on a non-default stream so the current overlap continues to hold under larger batch sizes.

## Detailed Analysis

### Compute Kernel Insights

<a id="detailed-analysis-compute-p1"></a>
<!-- reasoning-candidate tier=compute rank=1 -->
#### 🔴 P1: Compute-bound BF16 GEMMs underrunning roofline (Tensile)

**Identification:** 18 BF16 `aten::mm` shapes were flagged as the dominant GEMM cluster in the trace, accounting for 45.7 s of GPU kernel time (~80.6% of compute time). All flagged operations dispatch through the **Tensile** backend with `bound_type = compute`. The cluster spans the large MLP shapes (M=24576, K=8192, N=28672), the gate/up shapes (N=10240), the QKV/output shapes (N=8192), and the LM-head shapes (N=128256). (source: `gemm_metrics.json` → `category_findings[0].members[]`, `operations[].library`, `operations[].efficiency.bound_type`)

**Data:**

| Operation |  Args  |            Kernel Path                  | Time (ms) | %E2E | Count |FLOPS/Byte| Efficiency | Bound |
|-----------|--------|-----------------------------------------|-----------|------|-------|----------|------------|-------|
| aten::mm | (24576,8192) bf16<br>(8192,28672) bf16<br>(24576,28672) bf16 | — | 7607.463 | 13.42 | 320 | 5059.76 | 68.74% of 708 TFLOPS | compute-bound |

| aten::mm | (8192,24576) bf16<br>(24576,28672) bf16<br>(8192,28672) bf16 | — | 3206.531 | 5.65 | 160 | 5059.76 | 81.39% of 708 TFLOPS | compute-bound |

| aten::mm | (24576,8192) bf16<br>(8192,10240) bf16<br>(24576,10240) bf16 | — | 1239.131 | 2.19 | 160 | 3840.00 | 75.25% of 708 TFLOPS | compute-bound |
| aten::mm | (24576,10240) bf16<br>(10240,8192) bf16<br>(24576,8192) bf16 | — | 1124.109 | 1.98 | 160 | 3840.00 | 82.92% of 708 TFLOPS | compute-bound |
| aten::mm | (24576,8192) bf16<br>(8192,8192) bf16<br>(24576,8192) bf16 | — | 1007.500 | 1.78 | 160 | 3510.86 | 74.06% of 708 TFLOPS | compute-bound |
| aten::mm | (24576,8192) bf16<br>(8192,8192) bf16<br>(24576,8192) bf16 | — | 1005.523 | 1.77 | 160 | 3510.86 | 74.24% of 708 TFLOPS | compute-bound |
| aten::mm | (8192,24576) bf16<br>(24576,8192) bf16<br>(8192,8192) bf16 | — | 975.033 | 1.72 | 160 | 3510.86 | 76.47% of 708 TFLOPS | compute-bound |
| aten::mm | (24576,8192) bf16<br>(8192,8192) bf16<br>(24576,8192) bf16 | — | 861.230 | 1.52 | 160 | 3510.86 | 86.65% of 708 TFLOPS | compute-bound |
| aten::mm | (24576,8192) bf16<br>(8192,128256) bf16 | — | 190.720 | 0.34 | 2 | 5863.13 | 76.49% of 708 TFLOPS | compute-bound |
| aten::mm | (128256,24576) bf16<br>(24576,8192) bf16 | — | 174.651 | 0.31 | 2 | 5863.13 | 83.54% of 708 TFLOPS | compute-bound |
| aten::mm | (24576,128256) bf16<br>(128256,8192) bf16 | — | 170.869 | 0.30 | 2 | 5863.13 | 85.40% of 708 TFLOPS | compute-bound |

**Reasoning for Slowdown:** Every flagged shape has very high arithmetic intensity (FLOPS/Byte 3510–5863), so each GEMM is correctly compute-bound against the BF16 matrix-FP roofline (resolved peak 708 TFLOPS) rather than HBM-bound. The achieved TFLOPS/s sit between 486.7 and 613.5, which is 68.7%–86.7% of peak — the heaviest shape (`(24576,8192) × (8192,28672)`, 7.6 s of kernel time, count = 320) lands at only 68.7%, and a second 6.6 s instance of the same shape only reaches 79.0%, indicating that the same logical GEMM is hitting more than one Tensile kernel and at least one of those is sub-optimal. The smaller K=8192, N=8192 attention-projection shapes show the same pattern (74.1% / 74.2% / 76.5% on three 1 s clusters of identical `(24576,8192) × (8192,8192)`), and the lowest-efficiency shape on the gate/up path (`(24576,8192) × (8192,10240)`, 69.7%) reinforces that the gap is shape- and kernel-specific rather than a global ceiling. Decomposition strategy not visible — profile the kernel for tiling layout. Tile size not visible — profile the kernel for tile-size tuning.

**Resolution:** Tile / wave-occupancy tuning targets the specific Tensile kernels selected for these shapes so the same FLOPs are issued under a better-utilized MFMA pipeline, raising achieved TFLOPS/s without changing the algorithm. Narrowing precision (BF16 → FP8 or FP4, where the model tolerates it) doubles or quadruples the matrix roofline (708 → 1273 TFLOPS at FP8, and higher at FP4), which directly lowers the compute floor for these shapes since they are compute-bound, not memory-bound. The two-invocation LM-head and small-K shapes (count = 2) amortize per-launch overhead poorly relative to their compute; batching upstream reduces launch overhead's share of their total time. Bottleneck identified — generate reproducer for kernel team for the lowest-efficiency shapes (68.7%, 69.7%, 74.0%) so the Tensile selector can be revisited for those tile/M-N-K combinations.

<a id="detailed-analysis-compute-p2"></a>

#### 🟡 P2: Flash Attention forward underperforming the expected efficiency band at N=8192 (CK)

**Identification:** Two `flash_attn::_flash_attn_forward` groups (160 invocations each, 320 total) account for 4017.181 ms (7.08% of E2E GPU time) and both run on the **CK** backend with `is_flash_attention=true`. The workload is a GQA pattern (`gqa_ratio=8`, H_Q=64 over H_KV=8) at sequence length `N=8192` with causal masking. Both groups are compute-bound at ~37% of the resolved bf16 matrix peak (708 TFLOPS), below the 50–70% band typically expected for `N > 4096` (source: `sdpa_fwd_metrics.json` → `operations[].name`, `operations[].count`, `operations[].time_ms`, `operations[].efficiency.efficiency_percent`, `operations[].efficiency.bound_type`, `operations[].library`, `operations[].classification.is_flash_attention`, `operations[].classification.workload_profile`).

**Data:**

| Operation |  Args  |            Kernel Path                  | Time (ms) | %E2E | Count |FLOPS/Byte| Efficiency | Bound |
|-----------|--------|-----------------------------------------|-----------|------|-------|----------|------------|-------|
| flash_attn::_flash_attn_forward | (3,8192,64,128) bf16<br>(3,8192,8,128) bf16<br>(3,8192,8,128) bf16 | — | 2014.958 | 3.55 | 160 | 3640.89 | 37.03% of 708 TFLOPS | compute-bound |
| flash_attn::_flash_attn_forward | (3,8192,64,128) bf16<br>(3,8192,8,128) bf16<br>(3,8192,8,128) bf16 | — | 2002.223 | 3.53 | 160 | 3640.89 | 37.28% of 708 TFLOPS | compute-bound |

**Reasoning for Slowdown:** The kernel is compute-bound (FLOPS/byte = 3640.89, far above the bf16 ridge point) yet only realizes ~37% of the 708 TFLOPS bf16 matrix peak. At `N = 8192` (>4096 band) we would expect 50–70% — the achieved 262–264 TFLOPS sits about a third below that band, so memory-overhead dominance from short sequences does not explain the gap. The trace shows the bulk of time inside a single `ck_tile::FmhaFwdKernel` invocation per call (median ~12.55 ms, std-dev under 4%), so the underperformance is steady-state across the 160 invocations and not driven by tail variance. Flash tile size not visible — profile the kernel for tile-size tuning.

**Resolution:** Tile-size and pipeline-stage tuning of the CK Flash forward kernel directly increases MAC throughput per cycle on this fixed shape, which is the dominant cost in a compute-bound regime. The GQA 8:1 head ratio means each KV head is shared across 8 query heads, so the kernel must broadcast K/V tiles efficiently — sub-optimal tile shapes for the GQA broadcast pattern can leave matrix units idle and depress achieved TFLOPS, which is consistent with the observed gap below the expected band. Bottleneck identified — generate reproducer for kernel team.

**Impact estimate:**
<!-- impact-begin kind=detail_estimate low=3.34 high=4.45 -->
- Low end impact_score: 3.34
- High end impact_score: 4.45
<!-- impact-end -->

<a id="detailed-analysis-compute-p3"></a>
<!-- reasoning-candidate tier=compute rank=1 -->
#### 🟢 P3: Flash Attention backward at 54.58% of bf16 compute peak (CK)

**Identification:** All 160 sdpa_bwd invocations are served by Flash Attention backward (`flash_attn::_flash_attn_backward`), which dispatches to the **CK** backend. The op is classified compute-bound with FLOPs/byte = 5851.44, well above the bf16 ridge point. Achieved throughput is 386.4 TFLOPS against a 708 TFLOPS bf16 matrix peak (54.58%). The shape is a Llama-style GQA configuration (H_Q=64, H_KV=8, ratio 8:1) at sequence length 8192 — note GQA reduces KV-cache traffic but can slightly lower kernel efficiency vs. plain MHA. Coefficient of variation across the 160 calls is 0.009 (very stable). (source: `sdpa_bwd_metrics.json` → `operations[].efficiency.efficiency_percent`, `operations[].efficiency.bound_type`, `operations[].library`, `operations[].classification`).

**Data:**

| Operation |  Args  |            Kernel Path                  | Time (ms) | %E2E | Count |FLOPS/Byte| Efficiency | Bound |
|-----------|--------|-----------------------------------------|-----------|------|-------|----------|------------|-------|
| flash_attn::_flash_attn_backward | (3,8192,64,128) bf16<br>(3,8192,64,128) bf16<br>(3,8192,8,128) bf16<br>(3,8192,8,128) bf16<br>(3,8192,64,128) bf16<br>(3,64,8192) fp32<br>(3,8192,64,128) bf16<br>(3,8192,8,128) bf16<br>(3,8192,8,128) bf16<br>(2,) long int | — | 3414.968 | 6.02 | 160 | 5851.44 | 54.58% of 708 TFLOPS | compute-bound |

**Reasoning for Slowdown:** The backward is dispatching the optimized fused Flash Attention kernel (no unfused softmax/bmm pattern is present), so the slowdown is not algorithmic. The kernel-time breakdown is dominated by `kernel_func` (3153.3 ms across 160 calls, ~92% of the op's GPU time) — the Flash Attention backward main kernel — with the remaining ~8% spent in supporting CK kernels (`FmhaBwdOGradDotO`, `FmhaBwdConvertQGrad`) and small reductions/fills. Backward is generally less efficient than forward because it must recompute attention weights and move more bytes (dQ, dK, dV gradients), and at this shape achieved 386.4 TFLOPS sits ~45% below the bf16 matrix roofline. Trace data shows WHAT (efficiency gap) but not WHY at the micro-architecture level — Flash internal tile size is not visible from the trace.

**Resolution:** Kernel-level tuning of the dominant `kernel_func` (tile sizes, pipeline depth, register/LDS budget for the GQA 8:1 head ratio at d=128) is the lever that can close the gap to the 708 TFLOPS bf16 roofline, because at compute-bound operating points the kernel's effective MAC throughput is set by how well its tiling matches the matrix-core issue rate — not by anything visible from the trace. Flash tile size not visible — profile the kernel for tile-size tuning. Bottleneck identified — generate reproducer for the CK kernel team.

**Impact estimate:**
<!-- impact-begin kind=detail_estimate low=2.05 high=2.74 -->
- Low end impact_score: 2.05
- High end impact_score: 2.74

### System-Level Insights

<a id="detailed-analysis-system-p1"></a>
<!-- reasoning-candidate tier=system rank=1 -->
#### 🔴 P1: H2D memcpy hygiene check

**Identification:** The memcpy assessment flagged H2D transfers because the count (490) exceeds the threshold of 10, even though their aggregate time (14.411 ms) is only 0.03% of the 56,703.677 ms total GPU time. The memcpy overlap ratio is 0.002 (i.e., effectively all memcpy time runs concurrently with compute), so this is a count-threshold trip rather than a time-on-critical-path issue (source: `multi_kernel_metrics.json` → `memcpy_assessment.issues[].direction == "H2D"`, `overlap_analysis.memcpy_overlap_ratio`, `overlap_analysis.exposed_memcpy_time_us`).

**Data:**

| Metric | Value | Flagged |
|--------|-------|---------|
| H2D count | 490 | true (count > 10) |
| H2D total time | 14.411 ms | false (0.03% of E2E) |
| H2D avg bytes | 613,949 | — |
| Memcpy overlap ratio | 0.998 (1 − 0.002) | false |
| Exposed memcpy time | 14.442 ms (0.025% of E2E) | false |
| Exposed comm time | 240.873 ms (0.42% of E2E) | false |
| Compute/comm overlap | 98.6% | false (target > 70%) |

**Reasoning for Slowdown:** The trace shows there is no slowdown attributable to memcpy or communication. Computation occupies 99.30% of the timeline, exposed communication is 0.42%, exposed memcpy is 0.03%, and idle is 0.25%. The 490 H2D events are the per-step input-staging fan-in (avg ~614 KB each, ~287 MB total) and are scheduled concurrently with kernels on the compute stream, so they do not extend the critical path.

**Resolution:** No corrective action is needed for performance. The reason to still surface this finding is forward-looking: if batch shapes grow or the producer of these host buffers stops using pinned memory, the same 490 transfers would lose their async/overlap property and begin serializing against compute. Validating that host buffers are pinned and that copies are submitted on a side stream preserves the current 99.8% memcpy overlap as the workload scales.

**Impact estimate:** Impact estimate is not quantifiable from trace data.
